title: Regarding naming a specific name for jupyter notebook and different versions of notebook
body:
Hello,
In the terminal, if i type jupyter notebook, it will connect to a server and opens an untitled.ipynb and if i want to close the kernel, then in the terminal if  i type cntrl+c and then y, the kernel closes. Next time if i want to open a new notebook, then it will be automatically named as Untitled1.ipynb.
So,
1) How can i assign a specific name for the notebook i want to run (such that if i name each .ipynb files differently, it is easy for identification...)
2) For running jupyter notebook, it should connect every time to the server only..?? Is there no possibility to just open within the system (if opened in the server there is a chance of data breaching..??) or sometimes if there is no internet, then it is not possible to run the jupyter notebook right.?

How do i solve these issues..??

Any suggestions are appreciated.

Thank you.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
When you're in a notebook, you can click on the name (*Untitled*) at the top of the page to change it.

It opens in your browser, but it is actually running on your own computer. The URL should start with something like `http://localhost:8888` - *localhost* means your own computer. It's convenient for us to use HTML for the interface.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: The new interface you're using there is JupyterLab, which is in beta. If you need to switch back to the classic interface, you can change the URL from `/lab` to `/tree`.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Running ```jupyter notebook <filename.ipynb>``` launches it in lab, while ```jupyter notebook``` launches the classic notebook.
Is it possible to restore the default behaviour of ```jupyter notebook <filename.ipynb>``` command, i.e. starting classic jupyter notebook, not jupyter lab?

Or every time i launch the notebook  ```jupyter notebook <filename.ipynb>``` i should change the URL from ```/lab``` to ```/tree``` in order to get the classic notebook interface...?? and if i run any code/do any modifications and save it will it be saved correctly..??

Any suggestions...?

Thank you.
